findings.title: Gitleaks scanner unavailable
findings.description: Gitleaks is not installed or is not available on PATH, so local secret scanning was not run.
findings.risk: Secrets may exist in the target repository without being detected by this local scan.
findings.recommendation: Install Gitleaks and rerun `launchguardian scan --target .` before relying on scan results.

findings.title: Frontend-exposed secret-like environment variable
findings.description: Frontend-exposed environment variable name `NEXT_PUBLIC_SECRET_FAKE` looks secret-bearing. Variable values are not included in findings.
findings.risk: Frontend public environment variables are bundled for browser access and must not contain secrets.
findings.recommendation: Move the secret to server-side configuration and expose only non-sensitive public values to frontend code.

findings.title: Frontend debug or non-production URL reference
findings.description: Frontend file references `localhost`, which may indicate debug or non-production configuration.
findings.risk: Debug, localhost, or staging references can leak implementation context or break production behavior.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the reference is intentional and gated from production builds where appropriate.

findings.title: Sensitive-looking browser storage usage
findings.description: Browser storage usage references sensitive-looking token, secret, password, JWT, or API key names.
findings.risk: Sensitive values in localStorage or sessionStorage can be exposed to browser-side script access.
findings.recommendation: Use safer session handling patterns and avoid storing sensitive credentials in browser storage.
